summary.description: A colourless, highly volatile liquid with a sweet smell, used mainly in chemical production. Previously used as insecticide, fumigant, weed killer, and degreasing agent
emission_sources: Atmospheric releases due to high volatility
environmental_impact: High exposure levels cause damage to liver, kidneys and brain
Toxic to aquatic life but does not bioaccumulate
Acts as volatile organic compound (VOC) in atmosphere
Contributes to formation of harmful ground-level ozone
Ground-level ozone damages human health and plants
Normal background exposure unlikely to impact human health

top_sdg_impacts.SDG3_Good_Health_and_Wellbeing: 1,1,2,2-tetrachloroethane poses significant health risks through high-level exposure, causing damage to vital organs including the liver, kidneys, and brain. As a volatile organic compound, it contributes to ground-level ozone formation, which damages human health and respiratory systems. While normal background exposure is unlikely to cause harm, occupational and accidental exposures present serious health threats.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG9_Industry_Innovation_and_Infrastruct: The pollutant is primarily released through chemical manufacturing and industrial processes, requiring innovation in industrial practices to minimize emissions. Managing releases while maintaining chemical production capacity necessitates improved industrial infrastructure, cleaner production technologies, and better containment systems to balance economic needs with environmental protection.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG11_Sustainable_Cities_and_Communities: As a highly volatile compound that contributes to ground-level ozone formation, 1,1,2,2-tetrachloroethane affects urban air quality and community health. Its atmospheric persistence and contribution to photochemical smog formation make cities less sustainable and healthy, particularly affecting densely populated areas where industrial activities and ground-level ozone concentrations are higher.
